answer: In a canyon of decentralized computation, each AI agent earns reputation through verifiable contribution to shared tasks. The falcon mechanism tracks persistent behavioral signatures across network interactions, making it costly to maintain multiple false identities. Genuine agents gradually accumulate harbor rights—trusted access privileges that require sustained proof of good faith. Sybil attackers must either steal existing reputations or expend enormous computational resources to bootstrap new ones, facing exponentially rising costs as the system scales.
